We're implementing story 3.4 "Cancel-Safe Capture Across All Tabs" (FR-11) for a Flutter app (Cerne, Clean Architecture, flutter_bloc). This is a cross-cutting hardening story on top of stories 3.1 (Text), 3.2 (Audio), 3.3 (Photo), which already built the Insertion Modal (bottom sheet with 3 tabs: Texto/Áudio/Foto) and partial cancel-safety per-tab.

Acceptance criteria for 3.4 (from epics.md):
1. Given a recording or OCR/transcription in progress, when I switch to a different Insertion Modal tab, then the in-flight capture is canceled outright — no partial Entry is created.
2. Given I back out of the modal mid-photo or stop a recording before tapping Salvar, when the modal closes, then no POST /entries call fires for the abandoned capture.
3. Given any of the three tabs, when a capture is interrupted, then it is the Insertion Modal's own internal tab state that resets — the three tabs remain internal states of one sheet, never nested sheets.

Also from the epic-3 context doc: "Opening the modal always resets all three tabs to idle/empty; switching tabs mid-capture cancels the in-flight capture outright."

I need you to read these files in full and report back precisely, with file:line references:

1. `lib/features/capture/presentation/widgets/insertion_modal.dart` (1506 lines) — focus especially on:
   - `InsertionModal.show()` and its try/finally cleanup of the three cubits (text/audio/photo)
   - The tab-switch listener/logic (how switching CaptureTab triggers cancel on the outgoing tab's cubit)
   - What happens when the modal is reopened — are all three cubits reset to idle/empty, or do they retain state from a previous session (e.g. if user closed mid-capture then reopens)?
   - Any `isSaving` cross-tab OR logic
2. `lib/features/capture/presentation/cubit/text_entry_cubit.dart` (142 lines) — full read. Does it have a `cancel()` method? Does switching away from Texto tab actually clear/reset typed text, or does text just persist silently (is that even a "capture in progress" the AC cares about, or is Text tab exempt since it's synchronous/no async op)?
3. `lib/features/capture/presentation/cubit/audio_entry_cubit.dart` (575 lines) — specifically the `cancel()` method and how it's invoked from the modal on tab-switch vs modal-close. Does `cancel()` reset state to idle properly in all paths (mid-recording, mid-transcribing)?
4. `lib/features/capture/presentation/cubit/photo_entry_cubit.dart` (454 lines) — specifically `cancel()` and how it's invoked on tab-switch vs modal-close, mid-pick vs mid-OCR.
5. Existing tests: `test/features/capture/presentation/widgets/insertion_modal_audio_test.dart`, any `insertion_modal_photo_test.dart`, `insertion_modal_text_test.dart` if it exists — specifically look for any test that already asserts "switching tabs cancels in-flight capture" or "closing modal mid-capture never calls entriesRepository.create" across ALL THREE tabs combined in one flow, vs tests that only check one tab in isolation.
6. Also check `test/features/capture/photo_entry_flow_e2e_test.dart` (new/untracked file) — what does it test already regarding cancel-safety end-to-end?

Then report, in under 500 words:
- What cancel-safety behavior is ALREADY correctly implemented per-tab (so we don't duplicate work)
- What SPECIFIC gaps remain relative to the 3 ACs above — e.g. is there a gap where reopening the modal after an abandoned capture doesn't reset state? Is there a gap in test coverage (no single test exercises cross-tab interruption across all 3 modalities in one flow)? Is there any code path where a tab switch does NOT call cancel() on the outgoing cubit?
- Exact file:line anchors for every finding, both the "already works" and the "gap" ones.

tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem. You can access any file directly by using this tool.
Assume this tool is able to read all files on the machine. If the User provides a path to a file assume that path is valid. It is okay to read a file that does not exist; an error will be returned.

Usage:
- The file_path parameter must be an absolute path, not a relative path
- By default, it reads up to 2000 lines starting from the beginning of the file
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.

- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

25-
26-## Technical Decisions
27-
28-- Two feature modules split the work: `features/entries/` owns the `Entry` entity, the `EntriesRepository` port (`create` + `read` only — no update/delete ever), and the entries `hive_ce` box. `features/capture/` owns the Insertion Modal UI, the on-device Whisper STT flow, and the OCR call, and holds no Entry data itself — it only consumes the abstract port from `entries/domain` (never imports `entries/data/` or `entries/presentation/`). 29-- `create` on the port is idempotent on `(origin, chatMessageId)`, though that specific guard only matters starting with RF10; this epic just needs to not violate the port's shape.
30-- Backend calls for this epic: `POST /entries` → function `entries-create`; `POST /media/ocr` → function `media-ocr` (the photo itself is not persisted server-side, only the extracted text comes back). 31-- Error handling: map the 13 backend error codes (plus the local-only `MalformedResponse`) to the one sealed `Failure` hierarchy already defined in `core/failure/`. The retry interceptor fires only for the 6 server `retryable:true` codes — OCR/payload failures are never auto-retried.

33-- The Insertion Modal's three tabs are internal states of one bottom sheet, never nested sheets; its entrance animation is the shared `sheetUp` (0.2s) choreography, with no other motion invented.

35-## UX & Interaction Patterns
36-
37-- Insertion Modal: three equal-width tabs (Texto/Áudio/Foto); only the active tab gets a filled `colorPrimary` background. A close ("x") control is always present. The modal opens on Texto by default.
